condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All transferable L1 gold-voting records report human absolute oral bioavailability at or above 46% (alprazolam 80–100% and SR 84–91%; estazolam 87%; brigatinib 46%; GSK1322322 57–77%; suvorexant 82%; clobazam 90%; ranitidine 54–58%; 2,4-D rapid/complete), so none provides affirmative evidence for F < 20%.
L2 context records are predominantly supportive (estazolam ~98–100% in mice; alprazolam XR 92%; ranitidine in cirrhosis 70%; 2,4-D virtually 100%; brigatinib orally bioavailable).

L4 analog absorption/solubility/permeability evidence is supportive: chloroquine is highly absorbed and freely soluble; amodiaquine HCl equilibrium solubility is 6.9–8.9 mg/mL across pH 1.0–6.4; midazolam shows high Caco-2 Papp (6.99×10^-5 cm/s).

L5 amodiaquine gut-wall evidence shows high Caco-2 permeability (~20×10^-6 cm/s), higher apical-to-basolateral transport than mefloquine, and only limited/saturable P-gp efflux (ER 1.3 at 10 µM, judged clinically insignificant), supporting no major gut-wall barrier for this 4-aminoquinoline chemotype.
L5 records for unrelated compounds (compound 34 ER 2.1; MW181 not a Pgp substrate; compounds 7/15 good permeability/low efflux) are not query-specific and do not alter the direction.
The only low-F record (alprazolam in rat B, F=0.045 at 12.5 mg/kg) is species- and dose-specific and does not provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence against the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct query-specific absolute oral bioavailability or matched oral/IV AUC measurement is available.
No query-specific human PK data; exact dose, formulation, prandial state, and species are unspecified.
L5 gut-wall records are for amodiaquine and other analogs, not the query itself; no query-specific intestinal metabolism or efflux measurement is available.
The query is highly ionized at physiological pH (neutral fraction 0.01), though logD 2.15 and low TPSA support adequate passive permeability; no direct query permeability measurement is available.
The query's non-aromatic carbocycle linker is not represented in the analog permeability/efflux records; its metabolic stability is unmeasured.
